info.name: KJT Foodie API
info.description:
# KJT Foodie API

Requests are grouped by module in build order. Auth is set once on the collection (Bearer `{{token}}`); each role folder overrides it with that role's token variable (`customerToken`, `vendorToken`, `riderToken`, `adminToken`). The OpenAPI contract `docs/api/openapi.yaml` is the master; if this collection and the contract disagree, fix the contract first.

Swagger UI: `{{host}}/docs`

## Response envelope

```json
// single item
{ "success": true, "data": { "id": "...", "status": "accepted" } }

// list (offset pagination)
{ "success": true, "data": [ ... ], "meta": { "page": 2, "limit": 20, "total": 135, "totalPages": 7, "hasNextPage": true, "hasPrevPage": true } }

// cursor list (feed, comments)
{ "success": true, "data": [ ... ], "meta": { "nextCursor": "20", "limit": 10, "total": 134 } }

// error
{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "Please check the highlighted fields.", "fieldErrors": { "email": "Enter a valid email address" }, "requestId": "b1f6..." } }
```

`message` is shown to users as-is. `fieldErrors` keys are dotted request paths (`address.line1`). Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header equal to `error.requestId`. `DELETE` returns 204 with no body.

## Error codes

| HTTP | Code(s) |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` (malformed request or JSON) |
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN`, `ACCOUNT_BANNED`, `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` (also for resources you may not see) |
| 409 | `CONFLICT` (generic), `ALREADY_SUBMITTED`, `NOT_APPROVED`, `TRIAL_USED`, `SAME_PLAN`, `DOWNGRADE_AT_RENEWAL`, `PAYMENT_REQUIRED`, `PLAN_LIMIT`, `INVALID_STATUS`, `OFFER_GONE`, `CANNOT_CANCEL` |
| 413 | `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (JSON bodies over 1 MB) |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR`; checkout quote: `VENDOR_PAUSED`, `VENDOR_CLOSED`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `ITEM_UNAVAILABLE`, `EMPTY_CART` |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` (general limit 300/min per IP) |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` (quote `requestId`) |

## Variables

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `host` | Server root, e.g. `http://localhost:4000` |
| `baseUrl` | `{{host}}/api/v1` |
| `customerToken`, `vendorToken`, `riderToken`, `adminToken` | Saved by the login tests (phase 6) |

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness and readiness checks. No auth, not rate limited. `GET /api/v1/health` is the contract path the frontend uses; `/health` and `/health/ready` stay at the server root for load balancers.

request.description:
Contract path for the frontend (`GET /api/v1/health`, tag System). Returns 200 while the process is running.

**Who can call it:** anyone (no auth).

**Response `data`:**
- `status` (string) — always `ok`
- `time` (string) — server time, ISO 8601 UTC
- `uptime` (integer) — seconds since the process started

**Side effects:** none.

Returns 200 when every dependency is reachable (MySQL now; Redis from phase 5), otherwise 503 with the error envelope. Load balancers should send traffic only to ready instances.

**Who can call it:** anyone (no auth).

**Response `data`:**
- `status` (string) — `ready`
- `checks` (object) — `mysql: "up"`

**Errors:** 503 `INTERNAL` when a dependency is down.

**Side effects:** none.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Sign-up, sign-in (password, OTP, Google), refresh, logout and password reset. Public except logout. The refresh token is an httpOnly cookie `kjt_refresh` (Path=/api/v1/auth, 30 days, rotated on every refresh); Postman keeps it in its cookie jar. Seeded accounts all use `password123`; every OTP outside production is `123456`. Rate limits: 5/min per IP per route; OTP requests also 5 per 10 min per phone.

request.description:
Creates a customer, vendor or rider account (admins are created by a super admin). Vendors and riders also get an empty profile with `approvalStatus: draft`. Sends a `verify` OTP by SMS; call **Verify OTP** with `purpose: verify` to sign in.

**Errors:** 409 `CONFLICT` with `fieldErrors.phone` / `fieldErrors.email` when already registered; 422 field errors. (FR-ACC-01)

item.name: Log in with email and password

request.description:
Returns `{ accessToken, user }` and sets the refresh cookie. Saves `customerToken`.

**Errors:** 401 `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`; 403 `ACCOUNT_BANNED` / `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`.
Seeded vendor (Mama Put Kitchen). Saves `vendorToken`.
Seeded rider. Saves `riderToken`.
Seeded super admin (all permissions). Saves `adminToken`. Other admins: support@, finance@, dispatch@, onboarding@kjtfoodie.test.

`purpose` is `login` (default) or `verify` (resend after sign-up). Outside production the code is always `123456` and the SMS is only logged.

**Errors:** 422 `fieldErrors.phone` for an invalid or unknown number; 403 blocked account; 429 rate limited.

Checks the code and starts a session (marks the phone verified). A code works once and stops after 5 wrong tries.

**Errors:** 422 `fieldErrors.code`.

Verifies the Google ID token against `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`. Signs in the linked account, links an existing account with the same verified email, or creates a customer. (FR-ACC-05)

**Errors:** 401 invalid token; 403 blocked account.
Uses the `kjt_refresh` cookie; rotates it and returns a new session. 401 means signed out (the cookie is cleared). Replaying an already-rotated token revokes that whole sign-in.
Sends a reset code by email or SMS (to whichever the identifier is). Always the same answer, so it never reveals whether an account exists.

Sets the new password and signs the account out everywhere.

**Errors:** 422 `fieldErrors.code` / `fieldErrors.password`.
Revokes the refresh cookie's sign-in and clears the cookie. Works with an expired access token. Always 204.

item.description: The signed-in user and their saved addresses.

request.description: The signed-in user with fresh `permissions` (admins), `vendor { id, name, slug, approvalStatus, subscriptionStatus, planId, onboardingStep, logo }` (vendors) and `rider { id, approvalStatus, isOnline }` (riders). Any role.
Send only the fields that change: `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `avatar` (URL from POST /uploads). 409 when the email belongs to another account.

Customers only (403 for other roles). Removes personal data (name → "Deleted user", email / phone cleared, addresses deleted), keeps orders anonymised, signs out everywhere. NDPA 2023. **Destructive: run against a throwaway account.**
Customer only. Default first.

item.name: Admin · Users, roles and audit log
item.description: Admin accounts and the editable sub-role permission sets (handoff section 2). Uses `adminToken` (log in as super admin first).

request.description:
Page of `{ id, name, email, adminRole, status, createdAt }`. Search: name, email. Filters: `adminRole`, `status`. Default sort `name`.

**Permission:** `admin_users.manage` (super admin by default). 403 for other admins and non-admins.

Creates the admin without a password and emails a code (valid 3 days) with a link to the set-password page; they finish with POST /auth/password/reset. 422 field errors, including `email: That email already has an account`.

**Permission:** `admin_users.manage` (super admin by default). 403 for other admins and non-admins.

Change another admin's `adminRole` and / or `status` (`active` | `suspended`; suspended admins are blocked at once). 409 for yourself, 404 for non-admins.

**Permission:** `admin_users.manage` (super admin by default). 403 for other admins and non-admins.

item.name: Uploads
item.description:
`POST /uploads` (multipart `file` + `purpose`). Pick a file in the `file` field before sending. Returns `{ url, width, height, bytes }`; send `url` in the usual fields (`photos`, `logo`, `cover`, `documents[].url`, refund `photos`).

JPG / PNG / WebP (+ PDF for documents), max 8 MB → 413. Images are re-encoded to WebP (EXIF rotation applied, metadata stripped), under 2 MB. Wrong file type → 422 `fieldErrors.file`; purpose not allowed for your role → 403.
